title: Unstable AF: synchronised cardioversion
stem: Resus 2. A 65-year-old woman has had palpitations, chest tightness and breathlessness for 2 hours. HR 160 irregular, BP 80/50, RR 26, SpO2 93%, GCS 15 but sweaty and frightened. An IV cannula is in. Manage her tachyarrhythmia.

phases.title: ABC
phases.goal: Get her monitored, then assess her yourself: is she unstable? Read the ECG.

phases.title: Decide
phases.goal: Adverse features: what is the treatment, and does the AF duration change it?

phases.title: Prepare
phases.goal: Consent, a skilled sedationist with airway kit, sedation and heparin from the drug cart.

phases.title: Cardiovert
phases.goal: Use the defibrillator yourself: pads, SYNC, energy, all clear, shock.

phases.title: After
phases.goal: Reassess, look for the cause, and plan anticoagulation. Then the examiner.

events.say: She is greyer and more confused. BP 70/40.

review.text: Energies. AHA (as your notes and Hong Kong ACLS courses): 200 J synchronised for AF, 100 J for flutter and regular narrow complex tachycardia. RCUK/ERC: a high first shock for AF, 70–120 J for flutter and regular narrow complex. The script says 200 J, which both accept for AF.
AHA 2025 and RCUK 2025 wording is quoted from memory; the scored points are unchanged from the 2020/2021 algorithms.

notes:
Checked against Resuscitation Council UK 2025 (tachycardia algorithm; 2021 algorithm unchanged in principle), ESC 2024 AF guidelines and AHA 2025 ACLS.

Adverse features (RCUK): shock, syncope, myocardial ischaemia, severe heart failure. Any of these in a tachyarrhythmia → synchronised DC cardioversion, up to 3 attempts, under sedation or anaesthesia by someone skilled; then amiodarone 300 mg IV over 10–20 minutes and repeat the shock; then 900 mg over 24 hours.

Energy for AF: your notes use AHA 2025 (200 J biphasic for AF and flutter, 100 J for narrow regular and monomorphic VT; escalate). ERC/RCUK suggest a high initial energy for AF (at or near maximum, commonly 150–200 J), and 70–120 J for regular narrow complex tachycardia and flutter. The station accepts a high initial energy for AF and scores sync mode, safety and re-sync.

Haemodynamic instability overrides the usual 48-hour anticoagulation rule: give heparin at the time of cardioversion if it does not delay it. Never shock unsynchronised for AF: a shock on the T wave can cause VF. Adenosine has no role in AF. Rate-control calcium channel blockers or beta-blockers are dangerous in hypotension.

Perfect script checked against an AHA unstable tachycardia checklist, the RCUK tachycardia algorithm, an HKCEM-style scheme and a keyword scheme. Added: the adverse features named aloud (both lists), the 48-hour rule overridden, the plan if cardioversion fails, a cause looked for, and admission.

Bedside checks (pulse, ABCDE, reassessment) are done at the patient, with close-ups, not said to the nurse.

steps.label: Assess
steps.hint: ABCDE and the adverse features; a 12-lead if it doesn't delay.

ABCDE.r: Talking. RR 26, fine basal crackles. "Signs of heart failure."
ABCDE.mark: Assesses A and B: signs of heart failure

ABCDE.r: HR 160 irregularly irregular, BP 80/50, cool peripheries, CRT 4 s. "She is hypotensive and shocked."

ABCDE.t: Do you have any chest pain?
ABCDE.r: Tight central chest pain since it started. "Ischaemic chest pain."

ECG.r: Irregularly irregular narrow complex tachycardia, no P waves, rate about 160: AF with fast ventricular response. Rate-related ST depression.
ECG.mark: Interprets AF with fast ventricular response

steps.label: Decide
steps.hint: Name the adverse features; synchronised DC cardioversion now; instability overrides the 48-hour rule.

opts.t: She's unstable: hypotension and shock, ischaemic chest pain and heart failure. These are adverse features.
She needs synchronised DC cardioversion now.

steps.label: Talk to her
steps.hint: Explain the shock and take verbal consent.

opts.t: Hello Mrs Kwan, I'm the emergency doctor. Your heart is racing and your blood pressure is low. I'd like to give you medicine to make you sleepy and give your heart a small electric shock to reset its rhythm. Is that all right?
opts.tz: 關太你好，我係急症室醫生。你個心跳得好快，血壓又低。我想幫你打啲藥令你瞓一陣，再用電擊幫個心跳返正常。可唔可以？
opts.r: Yes, please. Just make it stop.
opts.rz: 好，唔該你，快啲整返好佢。

steps.label: Defibrillator

opts.performHint: She is sedated. Place both pads, SYNC on and check the markers on the R waves, 200 J for AF, CHARGE, ALL CLEAR, SHOCK.
mark: Synchronised mode confirmed on the R waves
Safe delivery: all clear, hold until discharge

steps.label: Reassess her
steps.hint: Rhythm and pulse, then ABCDE again and a 12-lead.

After the shock.t: The rhythm on the monitor, and her pulse
After the shock.r: Sinus rhythm at 84; radial pulse present; BP 118/72. "Converted to sinus rhythm."
Rousing from sedation, airway clear; RR 18, crackles settling, SpO2 97%; warm; chest pain eased.
Sinus rhythm 84; the ST depression has resolved.

steps.label: After
steps.hint: Reassess; re-sync; the plan if it fails; causes; anticoagulation; admit.

opts.t: SYNC re-selected before any further shock.
If it hadn't worked: re-sync, escalate the energy, up to three attempts, then amiodarone 300 mg over 10 to 20 minutes and shock again.
opts.mark: States the plan if cardioversion fails

opts.t: Bloods for potassium, magnesium, thyroid function and troponin; look for a cause such as sepsis or ischaemia.
opts.mark: Looks for causes: electrolytes, thyroid, ischaemia

opts.t: Long-term anticoagulation decided by her CHA2DS2-VA score.
Admit her to a monitored bed under cardiology, and tell her how it went.

qs.a: Shock, syncope, myocardial ischaemia, heart failure
wrong: Rate over 100 with palpitations and anxiety
Fever, rash, vomiting and abdominal pain

qs.q: Why must the shock be synchronised?
qs.a: To avoid a shock on the T wave (R-on-T VF)
wrong: It uses less energy per shock
It is less painful than an unsynchronised shock
It only works if the patient is in sinus rhythm

qs.a: Amiodarone 300 mg over 10–20 min, then shock
wrong: Adenosine 12 mg, then a fourth synchronised shock
Switch to an unsynchronised 360 J shock
Stop, rate-control, and observe on the ward

qs.q: When is an unsynchronised shock appropriate?
wrong: Fast AF with a rate over 180

qs.q: AF for 2 hours with shock — do you wait for anticoagulation?
qs.a: No: give heparin and cardiovert now
wrong: Yes, a TOE must exclude clot first
Only if the CHA2DS2-VA score is zero

rules.fail: Shocked before deciding it was needed.

badge.name: In Sync
badge.flavor: Adverse features mean electricity. SYNC on, markers on the R waves.

options: Oral beta-blocker and review in clinic

cards.q: AHA 2025 initial synchronised energy for AF?
cards.note: ERC/RCUK: high initial energy for AF.

cards.q: Initial energy for regular narrow complex SVT (AHA)?
Amiodarone loading dose in unstable tachycardia after failed shocks?
options: 150 mg as a rapid bolus push

cards.q: Why is adenosine not useful in AF?
options: The AV node is not part of the AF circuit
It is only licensed for ventricular tachycardia
It precipitates VF in most patients with AF
Its half-life is too long for a fast rhythm
cards.why: It may transiently slow the ventricular rate but will not convert AF.

cards.q: Before each repeat synchronised shock you must…
cards.why: Many devices default to unsynchronised after a shock.

script.say: Hello Mrs Kwan, I'm the emergency doctor. Monitoring on, please: ECG, blood pressure every 3 minutes and SpO2, and oxygen to keep her 94 to 98%.

ABCDE. She's talking. Respiratory rate 26 with fine basal crackles: signs of heart failure. Heart rate 160 irregularly irregular, BP 80/50, cool, capillary refill 4 seconds: she's hypotensive and shocked. Do you have any chest pain?
script.do: Tight central chest pain since it started.
AF with fast ventricular response at about 160; rate-related ST depression.

script.say: She's unstable: hypotension and shock, ischaemic chest pain and heart failure. These are adverse features. She needs synchronised DC cardioversion now.
Instability overrides the 48-hour rule: we don't wait for anticoagulation or an echo; heparin at the time of the shock.
Please call the anaesthetist or a skilled sedationist; airway kit, suction and oxygen ready.
Mrs Kwan, your heart is racing and your blood pressure is low. I'd like to give you medicine to make you sleepy and give your heart a small electric shock to reset its rhythm. Is that all right?
Ketamine 0.5 mg per kg IV, titrated, to keep her pressure up. Unfractionated heparin 5000 units IV.
Pads on. SYNC on: markers on the R waves. 200 joules. Charging. Oxygen away, all clear: shocking, holding until it discharges.
script.do: Pads anterolateral; SYNC; 200 J; charge; all clear; shock.

script.say: Rhythm and pulse check: sinus rhythm at 84. SYNC re-selected before any further shock. If it hadn't worked: re-sync, escalate the energy, up to three attempts, then amiodarone 300 mg over 10 to 20 minutes and shock again.
Repeat ABCDE and a 12-lead ECG. Bloods for potassium, magnesium, thyroid function and troponin; look for a cause such as sepsis or ischaemia.
Long-term anticoagulation decided by her CHA2DS2-VA score. Admit her to a monitored bed under cardiology, and tell her how it went.
